data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'W-D-D', meaning love, affection, kindness, and compassion. In Islamic context, it represents the divine love and mercy bestowed upon believers. The name Mawadda carries the meaning “Love, Compassion” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Mawadda usually hope their child will grow to embody love, compassion and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: Mawadda is a name that carries deep cultural significance in the Islamic world. It is considered to be a noble, virtuous, and beautiful name reminiscent of love, kindness, and compassion. Naming a child as Mawadda is an expression of the hope that they will grow up to be loving and kind individuals, spreading positivity and warmth around them, reflecting the values of kindness and compassion that are highly valued in Islamic culture.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic tradition, Mawadda is associated with divine love and mercy. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) described God as "Ar-Rahman Ar-Rahim," meaning "The Most Merciful, The Compassionate." Mawadda represents the human expression and manifestation of this divine love and mercy. By embodying the spirit of Mawadda, Muslims are reminded to cultivate a deep sense of love and compassion towards all of God's creation, and to strive towards creating a more loving and compassionate world. This name, thus, holds immense spiritual significance as it helps to remind believers of their connection to the Ultimate Source of Love and Mercy - God Almighty.
